🎬 Tired of heavy, subscription-bound video editors holding back your workflows? Say hello to FilmCraft: an ambitious, clean-room reimplementation of Adobe Premiere Pro written in pure Rust! 🦀⚡️

Whether you are a systems developer, a Rust engineer, or an AI builder, FilmCraft delivers native, high-performance non-linear video editing across desktop platforms and the browser via WebAssembly—completely free of proprietary dependencies.

Here is what makes FilmCraft a game-changer for developers and creators:
• Custom Codecs: Built directly from public specifications for H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and AAC.
• Exact-Integer Time Math: Operates on 254,016,000,000 ticks per second to eliminate edit drift across any frame rate or sample rate.
• Cross-Platform & Web: Native support on macOS, Windows, and Linux, plus seamless web deployment via WebAssembly.
• AI-Agent Native: Every single action in the application is designed as a precise, programmatic command, making it ideal for automated video-generation pipelines.

Dive into a pristine, modular codebase to study real-world multimedia rendering, linear-light GPU compositing, and precise temporal math. Embed a professional-grade timeline directly into your own web or desktop applications today!

👉 Check out the repo and leave a star: https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft

Stop wasting hours writing complex WebGL boilerplate just to add a smooth gradient or background blur to your web apps. 

Drop high-performance WebGPU shader effects directly into your React, Vue, Svelte, or Solid apps using a familiar declarative component tree! 🚀

Building modern web aesthetics usually means wrestling with low-level graphics code and a steep learning curve. This open-source project bridges next-generation WebGPU performance with your favorite frontend frameworks, letting you add buttery-smooth, hardware-accelerated visuals without the usual headaches.

✨ Key Features You'll Love:
• Cross-Framework Power: First-class support for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and vanilla JS using identical component props.
• Declarative GPU Layers: Nest effects, blend them top-to-bottom, and apply masks natively inside the DOM.
• Visual Design Editor: Use the companion editor at shaders.com to design effects on an infinite canvas and export exact component trees.
• AI MCP Server Integration: Seamlessly use coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf to find, install, and edit shaders directly via the Model Context Protocol.
• Over 200+ Components: Ready-to-use gradients, lighting, blurs, and distortions for hero sections, interactive cursor trails, and SaaS dashboards.

Check out the repository and level up your UI/UX today:

📸 Tired of proprietary ecosystems holding your professional RAW photo processing hostage? 

Meet LightCraft: a clean-room, pure-Rust reimplementation of Adobe Lightroom designed to completely liberate your workflow while introducing native AI agent control. 

🧩 The Problem It Solves:
LightCraft delivers a complete, non-destructive photo library and RAW image development darkroom. It runs natively across macOS, Windows, and Linux, and even compiles to WebAssembly for seamless browser deployment—all while implementing a high-performance, wide-gamut, 32-bit float processing pipeline.

🚀 Notable Features:
- Scene-referred, wide-gamut, 32-bit float rendering pipeline for precise color and tone adjustments using OkLCh-based color grading.
- Comprehensive local masking suite featuring AI-ready subject, sky, and background detection alongside traditional gradient, brush, and luminance range tools.
- Built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enabling complete end-to-end control and automation of the photo editing workflow by AI agents.
- Smooth edge-aware local tone mapping built for maximum speed and cross-platform native performance.

💡 Why Developers Love It:
Study LightCraft as an advanced architectural reference for building high-performance image processing pipelines in Rust. Plus, the built-in MCP server provides a brilliant blueprint for integrating LLMs and AI agents directly into complex desktop software.

👉 Check out the repository and start exploring the code today:
https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft
